objects.description: No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only provides macro utilities (C linkage macros, boolean/NULL macros, and symbol visibility). Therefore, there are no user-defined types to document.

objects.definition:
typedef enum _SpectreStatus {
	SPECTRE_STATUS_SUCCESS               /*! No error */  = 0,
	SPECTRE_STATUS_NO_MEMORY             /*! There has been a problem 
	                                         allocating memory */,
	SPECTRE_STATUS_LOAD_ERROR            /*! There has been a problem 
	                                         loading the postcript file */,
	SPECTRE_STATUS_DOCUMENT_NOT_LOADED   /*! A function that needs the 
	                                         document to be loaded has been 
	                                         called and the document has not
	                                         been loaded or there was an 
	                                         error when loading it */,
	SPECTRE_STATUS_INVALID_PAGE          /*! The request page number
	                                         is not in the document page
	                                         range */,
	SPECTRE_STATUS_RENDER_ERROR          /*! There has been a problem
					         rendering the page */,
	SPECTRE_STATUS_EXPORTER_ERROR        /*! There has been a problem
					         exporting the document */,
	SPECTRE_STATUS_SAVE_ERROR            /*! There has been a problem
					         saving the document */
} SpectreStatus;
objects.description: Enumeration of error/status codes returned by Libspectre APIs. Values indicate success or specific failure categories (memory allocation, load, document state, invalid page, render, export, save). Used for reporting and branching on operation outcomes.

Opaque render-context handle used to control how a page is rendered in Libspectre (scale, rotation, DPI, page size, font usage, antialias settings). The struct is forward-declared and not defined in this header; it must be created and freed via the provided API.
Enumeration of page orientation values used by Libspectre to describe the intended rotation of a page. Includes portrait, reverse landscape ("seascape"), reverse portrait, and landscape.

Opaque handle representing a page of a PostScript document. Instances are not directly created by users; they are obtained from spectre_document_get_page (not defined in this header). The concrete structure layout is hidden.
Enumeration of output formats supported by the exporter: PostScript (PS) and PDF. Used to select the export target when creating an exporter.

Opaque exporter handle that performs document export to PS or PDF. It is created with spectre_exporter_new for a given SpectreDocument and format, used through begin/do_page/end, and destroyed with spectre_exporter_free. The actual struct layout is hidden (forward declaration only).

Opaque handle to a PostScript document within Libspectre. The struct is forward-declared here (no layout is exposed), indicating it is managed internally by the library. Create with spectre_document_new and release with spectre_document_free. Most operations can fail; check spectre_document_status after calls that can fail, as noted in the API comments.
No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only provides version macros and C linkage macros. Therefore, there are no custom data types to document.
Referenced via #include <libspectre/spectre-document.h>, but not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions.
Referenced via #include <libspectre/spectre-render-context.h>, but not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions.
Referenced via #include <libspectre/spectre-page.h>, but not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions.
Referenced via #include <libspectre/spectre-exporter.h>, but not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions.

functions.name: spectre_status_to_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable textual description for the given SpectreStatus code. Use it to convert Libspectre status/error codes into strings suitable for logs or messages. Notes: the returned pointer refers to a const character sequence; ownership/lifetime is not documented in this header, and NULL-return conditions (if any) are not specified.
requirements: The status argument must be a valid SpectreStatus enumeration value.
The returned string must be treated as read-only (do not modify its contents).

functions.name: spectre_render_context_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new SpectreRenderContext used to control how pages are rendered (scale, rotation, resolution, etc.). Typical usage is to create a context once, configure its parameters, use it for one or more render operations, and then free it with spectre_render_context_free.
requirements: Must be paired with spectre_render_context_free to avoid memory leaks.
Return value must be checked for NULL if the implementation can fail to allocate memory (unknown from header).

functions.name: spectre_render_context_free
functions.description: Free a SpectreRenderContext previously created with spectre_render_context_new. After this call the context must not be used.
requirements: rc must be a valid SpectreRenderContext previously returned by spectre_render_context_new (not already freed).
rc must not be used after this call (no use-after-free).
Should be called at most once per created context.
Behavior on rc == NULL is unknown; callers should pass a non-NULL pointer.

functions.name: spectre_render_context_set_scale
functions.description: Set the render scale factors for X and Y. Default is 1.0 for both. Use to zoom rendering independently in each axis.
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.
No explicit constraints on x_scale or y_scale are documented (valid ranges unknown).

functions.name: spectre_render_context_get_scale
functions.description: Retrieve the current X and Y scale factors. Either output pointer may be NULL to ignore that value.
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.
x_scale may be NULL; y_scale may be NULL.

functions.name: spectre_render_context_set_rotation
functions.description: Set the page rotation to apply during rendering. Default is 0 degrees. Common values are 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees.
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.
No explicit restriction on rotation values is documented; typical values are 0, 90, 180, 270 (non-restrictive note).

functions.name: spectre_render_context_get_rotation
functions.description: Get the current render rotation in degrees.
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.

functions.name: spectre_render_context_set_resolution
functions.description: Set the horizontal and vertical resolution (in DPI) used for rendering. Default is 72 DPI for both directions.
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.
No explicit constraints on x_dpi or y_dpi are documented (valid ranges unknown).

functions.name: spectre_render_context_get_resolution
functions.description: Retrieve the horizontal and vertical resolution (in DPI). Either output pointer may be NULL to ignore that value.
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.
x_dpi may be NULL; y_dpi may be NULL.

functions.name: spectre_render_context_set_page_size
functions.description: Set the page size in pixels. Rotation is automatically accounted for during rendering; this does not affect scale. If not set, the page bounding box or the slice rectangle will be used.
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.
No explicit constraints on width or height are documented (allowed ranges unknown).

functions.name: spectre_render_context_get_page_size
functions.description: Get the configured page size in pixels. Either output pointer may be NULL to ignore that value.
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.
width may be NULL; height may be NULL.

functions.name: spectre_render_context_set_use_platform_fonts
functions.description: Enable or disable the use of platform fonts when rendering. Default is TRUE (non-zero).
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.
use_platform_fonts is treated as a boolean flag (0 to disable, non-zero to enable); exact accepted values beyond this are not specified.

functions.name: spectre_render_context_get_use_platform_fonts
functions.description: Query whether platform fonts are enabled for rendering. Returns an int acting as a boolean flag (non-zero means enabled).
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.

functions.name: spectre_render_context_set_antialias_bits
functions.description: Set antialiasing settings for graphics and text. Typical values are 4 for graphics AA (1 = none) and 2 for text AA (1 = none).
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.
No explicit constraints on graphics_bits or text_bits are documented (allowed values unknown).

functions.name: spectre_render_context_get_antialias_bits
functions.description: Get the current antialias bit settings for graphics and text.
requirements: rc must be a valid, initialized SpectreRenderContext.
graphics_bits must be a non-NULL pointer.
text_bits must be a non-NULL pointer.

functions.name: spectre_page_status
functions.description: Returns the current status of the given SpectrePage. Typically used after rendering operations to determine whether the last action on the page succeeded or failed.
requirements: page must be a valid SpectrePage obtained from spectre_document_get_page and not yet freed.
Callers should check the returned SpectreStatus to handle failures from prior operations (e.g., render functions).
Thread-safety/usage across threads is unknown.

functions.name: spectre_page_free
functions.description: Frees the memory associated with the given SpectrePage. Pages cannot be created directly; they are obtained from spectre_document_get_page.
requirements: page must be a valid SpectrePage obtained from spectre_document_get_page.
Do not use the page pointer after calling this function (it becomes invalid).
Do not call this function more than once on the same page pointer (double free is undefined).
Ownership/lifetime of any data obtained from the page (e.g., label strings or rendered buffers) after freeing the page is unknown unless otherwise documented.

functions.name: spectre_page_get_index
functions.description: Returns the zero-based index of the page within its document (first page has index 0).
requirements: page must be a valid SpectrePage obtained from spectre_document_get_page and not yet freed.

functions.name: spectre_page_get_label
functions.description: Returns the label of the page in the document (if any). The label is a human-readable identifier separate from the numeric index.
requirements: page must be a valid SpectrePage obtained from spectre_document_get_page and not yet freed.
The ownership and lifetime of the returned const char* are not specified in this header; treat it as read-only. Whether the pointer remains valid after the page is freed is unknown.

functions.name: spectre_page_get_orientation
functions.description: Returns the page’s orientation as a SpectreOrientation value (Portrait, Landscape, Reverse Portrait, Reverse Landscape).
requirements: page must be a valid SpectrePage obtained from spectre_document_get_page and not yet freed.

functions.name: spectre_page_get_size
functions.description: Returns the page’s size (width and height) according to the page bounding box, ignoring page orientation. Either output pointer may be NULL to skip that value.
requirements: page must be a valid SpectrePage obtained from spectre_document_get_page and not yet freed.
width may be NULL if the width is not needed.
height may be NULL if the height is not needed.
Returned size values are independent of orientation; use spectre_page_get_orientation for orientation-aware layout.

functions.name: spectre_page_render
functions.signature: void spectre_page_render(SpectrePage *page, SpectreRenderContext *rc, unsigned char **page_data, int *row_length);
functions.description: Renders the entire page to an RGB32 pixel buffer. On success, page_data points to the image data and row_length receives the number of bytes per row. This function can fail; use spectre_page_status to check the result.
requirements: page must be a valid SpectrePage obtained from spectre_document_get_page and not yet freed.
rc must be a valid SpectreRenderContext configured with the desired rendering parameters (details not specified here).
page_data must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated image buffer pointer on success.
row_length must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of bytes per row.
The output format is RGB32; callers must respect row_length (it may differ from width*4).
On failure, callers should query spectre_page_status(page) to obtain the error status.
Ownership/allocation and how to free the returned page_data buffer are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: spectre_page_render_slice
functions.signature: void spectre_page_render_slice(SpectrePage *page, SpectreRenderContext *rc, int x, int y, int width, int height, unsigned char **page_data, int *row_length);
functions.description: Renders a rectangular slice of the page to an RGB32 pixel buffer. The rectangle is specified by the top-left coordinates (x, y) and its width and height. On success, page_data points to the image data and row_length receives the number of bytes per row. This function can fail; use spectre_page_status to check the result.
requirements: page must be a valid SpectrePage obtained from spectre_document_get_page and not yet freed.
rc must be a valid SpectreRenderContext configured with the desired rendering parameters (details not specified here).
x and y specify the top-left corner of the rectangle to render; the coordinate system and valid range are not specified here (unknown).
width and height should be positive integers (inferred from their use as dimensions).
page_data must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated image buffer pointer on success.
row_length must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of bytes per row.
The output format is RGB32; callers must respect row_length (it may differ from width*4).
On failure, callers should query spectre_page_status(page) to obtain the error status.
Ownership/allocation and how to free the returned page_data buffer are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: spectre_exporter_new
functions.description: Creates a new SpectreExporter instance for exporting the given SpectreDocument to the specified format (PS or PDF). Typical usage is to construct the exporter, then call spectre_exporter_begin, spectre_exporter_do_page for each page to export, and spectre_exporter_end before freeing the exporter.
requirements: document must be a valid, initialized SpectreDocument pointer referring to the document to export (ownership not transferred).
format must be a valid SpectreExporterFormat value (SPECTRE_EXPORTER_FORMAT_PS or SPECTRE_EXPORTER_FORMAT_PDF).
The returned SpectreExporter* must be released with spectre_exporter_free when no longer needed.
If allocation or initialization fails, NULL may be returned; callers should check for NULL before further use (inferred from common C API patterns; exact failure modes not documented).

functions.name: spectre_exporter_free
functions.description: Destroys and frees a SpectreExporter previously created with spectre_exporter_new, releasing any associated resources.
requirements: exporter must be a SpectreExporter* previously returned by spectre_exporter_new.
exporter must not have been freed already.
Behavior when exporter is NULL is unknown (not documented); callers should pass a valid pointer to be safe.

functions.name: spectre_exporter_begin
functions.description: Starts an export session, opening/creating the specified output file and preparing to write the exported document in the format configured for this exporter. Call before exporting pages and finish with spectre_exporter_end.
requirements: exporter must be a valid SpectreExporter* created by spectre_exporter_new.
filename must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated path string to the output file; the process must have permission to create or overwrite the file as needed (inferred from typical exporter semantics).
Must be called before spectre_exporter_do_page and spectre_exporter_end for a given exporter.
Return value is a SpectreStatus; callers must check and handle non-success statuses before proceeding (exact status codes defined by SpectreStatus in spectre-status.h).

functions.name: spectre_exporter_do_page
functions.description: Exports a single page from the associated SpectreDocument to the output begun with spectre_exporter_begin. Typically called once per page in the desired order.
requirements: exporter must be a valid SpectreExporter* for which spectre_exporter_begin has previously succeeded.

page_index must designate an existing page in the document; it must be within the document’s page count. Whether indexing is zero-based or one-based is not documented here; follow the library’s page-indexing convention used elsewhere (unknown in this header).
Must check the returned SpectreStatus and stop or handle errors appropriately before proceeding to additional pages or calling spectre_exporter_end.

functions.name: spectre_exporter_end
functions.description: Finishes the export session, flushing and finalizing the output file. Should be called after all desired pages have been exported via spectre_exporter_do_page.
requirements: exporter must be a valid SpectreExporter* for which spectre_exporter_begin has been called.
Should be called after exporting the intended pages; behavior if called without pages is unspecified in this header.
Return value is a SpectreStatus; callers must check and handle errors.
After successful completion, the exporter can be freed with spectre_exporter_free.

functions.name: spectre_document_new
functions.description: Create a new SpectreDocument handle representing a PostScript document. Use this before any other SpectreDocument operations.
requirements: Return value must be checked for NULL to detect allocation failure (not documented, but standard C API practice).
The returned SpectreDocument must later be released with spectre_document_free.

functions.name: spectre_document_load
functions.description: Load the given file into an existing SpectreDocument. On failure, the document’s status will report the error via spectre_document_status.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument created by spectre_document_new and not yet freed.
filename must reference a file to load. Exact path and encoding requirements are unknown.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should query spectre_document_status(document) to determine success or failure.

functions.name: spectre_document_status
functions.description: Return the current status code of the SpectreDocument. Typically used after operations that can fail to check for errors.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument created by spectre_document_new and not yet freed.

functions.name: spectre_document_free
functions.description: Free a SpectreDocument and release its associated resources.
requirements: document must be a SpectreDocument previously created by spectre_document_new.
document must not be used after this call (use-after-free is invalid).

functions.name: spectre_document_get_n_pages
functions.description: Return the number of pages in the document. On failure, consult spectre_document_status.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to confirm the result is valid.

functions.name: spectre_document_get_orientation
functions.description: Return the document’s orientation. On failure, consult spectre_document_status.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to confirm the result is valid.

functions.name: spectre_document_get_title
functions.description: Return the document title as a const string, or NULL if no title is specified. On failure, consult spectre_document_status. No ownership transfer is indicated.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
The returned pointer may be NULL if unset.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to confirm the result is valid.

functions.name: spectre_document_get_creator
functions.description: Return the document creator as a const string, or NULL if unspecified. On failure, consult spectre_document_status. No ownership transfer is indicated.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
The returned pointer may be NULL if unset.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to confirm the result is valid.

functions.name: spectre_document_get_for
functions.description: Return the document “for” field as a const string, or NULL if unspecified. On failure, consult spectre_document_status. No ownership transfer is indicated. Note: the field name appears to be a literal metadata key named "For".
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
The returned pointer may be NULL if unset.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to confirm the result is valid.

functions.name: spectre_document_get_creation_date
functions.description: Return the document’s creation date string copied verbatim from the file, or NULL if unspecified. No date format can be assumed. On failure, consult spectre_document_status. No ownership transfer is indicated.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
The returned pointer may be NULL if unset.
Date format is unspecified; callers must not assume a particular format.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to confirm the result is valid.

functions.name: spectre_document_get_format
functions.description: Return the document format as a const string. On failure, consult spectre_document_status. No ownership transfer is indicated.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to confirm the result is valid.
The returned pointer may be NULL on failure or if unspecified (not explicitly stated).

functions.name: spectre_document_is_eps
functions.description: Return nonzero if the document is an Encapsulated PostScript (EPS) file, zero otherwise. On failure, consult spectre_document_status.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to confirm the result is valid.

functions.name: spectre_document_get_language_level
functions.description: Return the PostScript language level of the document, or 0 if no level is defined. On failure, consult spectre_document_status.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to confirm the result is valid.

functions.name: spectre_document_get_page
functions.description: Return a SpectrePage for the given zero-based page index. On failure, consult spectre_document_status. Ownership/lifetime of the returned page is not specified here.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
page_index is zero-based; the first page has index 0.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to confirm the result is valid.
Lifetime and ownership rules for the returned SpectrePage are unknown from this header and should be verified in the SpectrePage API.

functions.name: spectre_document_get_page_by_label
functions.description: Return a SpectrePage referenced by a page label. On failure, consult spectre_document_status. Ownership/lifetime of the returned page is not specified here.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
label identifies a page; exact label format is unknown.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to confirm the result is valid.
Lifetime and ownership rules for the returned SpectrePage are unknown from this header and should be verified in the SpectrePage API.

functions.name: spectre_document_render_full
functions.description: Render the document using an explicit SpectreRenderContext. Intended for documents without pages (typically EPS); for multipage documents, the first page is rendered. On failure, consult spectre_document_status. Note: although the comment mentions width/height outputs, this signature only returns image data and row length; width/height retrieval is not part of this function’s parameters.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
rc must be a valid SpectreRenderContext configured as desired (initialization details are not provided here).
page_data must be a valid pointer to an unsigned char* where the function will store the rendered image buffer pointer.
row_length must be a valid pointer to int where the function will store the row length (in bytes).
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to determine success.
Ownership and lifetime of the returned image buffer via page_data are not specified here and should be verified in the render context or image API.

functions.name: spectre_document_render
functions.description: Render the document using default options (no explicit render context). Intended for documents without pages (typically EPS); for multipage documents, the first page is rendered. On failure, consult spectre_document_status.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
page_data must be a valid pointer to an unsigned char* where the function will store the rendered image buffer pointer.
row_length must be a valid pointer to int where the function will store the row length (in bytes).
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to determine success.
Ownership and lifetime of the returned image buffer via page_data are not specified here and should be verified in the library documentation.

functions.name: spectre_document_get_page_size
functions.description: Retrieve the page size for documents without pages (typically EPS). For multipage documents, returns the size of the first page. Callers may pass NULL for width or height to ignore that dimension.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
width may be NULL if the width is not needed; otherwise, must point to writable int.
height may be NULL if the height is not needed; otherwise, must point to writable int.

functions.name: spectre_document_save
functions.description: Save the document to the specified path. On failure, consult spectre_document_status.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
filename must be a path where the document will be saved; further format/permissions requirements are unknown.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to determine success.

functions.name: spectre_document_save_to_pdf
functions.description: Save the document as a PDF file at the specified path. On failure, consult spectre_document_status.
requirements: document must be a valid SpectreDocument.
filename must be a path where the PDF will be written; further format/permissions requirements are unknown.
This function can fail; after calling, the caller should check spectre_document_status(document) to determine success.

data_types.description: A path string to a file on the local filesystem. It may be absolute or relative and should be NUL-terminated. Used by APIs to open, read, write, or create files. The fuzzing harness provides an existing temporary path when used with FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.

File contents containing PostScript language data, including general PostScript or Encapsulated PostScript (EPS). May include typical PS headers, DSC comments, and page descriptions. Consumed by document loaders/parsers such as Libspectre.

A generic NUL-terminated byte string with no required structure or encoding. May be empty or contain any bytes except NUL; used where functions accept opaque labels or identifiers without a specified format.

generators.generator:
import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid filesystem path byte strings suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# Goals:
# - NUL-terminated C string when embedded by harness (we just return bytes; harness will use as file data for filename provider).
# - Cover absolute/relative, nested dirs, various extensions relevant to libspectre (ps, eps, pdf),
#   and names that exercise edge cases but are valid (spaces, unicode, long segments, dotfiles).
# - Keep total length <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic given the seed, but varied.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.#@+={}()[],$!^%~"

PS_EXTS = [".ps", ".eps", ".PS", ".EPS", ".Ps", ".pdf", ".PDF"]

# A small corpus of interesting base names
BASENAMES = [
    "doc",
    "empty",
    "sample",
    "unicode-αβγ",
    "longname-" + ("a" * 60),
    ".hidden",
    "CON" if os.name == "nt" else "aux-file",
    "NUL" if os.name == "nt" else "nul-file",
    "page-0001",
    "with space",
    "semi;colon",
]

# Interesting directory components
DIR_PARTS = [
    "tmp",
    "var",
    "home",
    "usr",
    "opt",
    "build",
    "..",
    ".",
    "nested",
    "深い",
    "スペクトル",
    "pages",
    "export",
]

def _rand_ext(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(PS_EXTS)

def _rand_component(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # generate a safe filename component (no path separators)
    base_choice = rng.choice(BASENAMES)
    # randomly augment with random chars
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        extra_len = rng.randint(0, 12)
        extra = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(extra_len))
        base_choice = f"{base_choice}{extra}"
    # avoid empty component
    if not base_choice:
        base_choice = "file"
    # strip leading/trailing spaces randomly
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base_choice = base_choice.strip()
        if not base_choice:
            base_choice = "name"
    return base_choice

def _build_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide absolute vs relative
    is_abs = rng.random() < 0.5
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Root prefix depending on platform semantics; use POSIX style for fuzzer portability
    prefix = "/" if is_abs else ""

    # Depth
    depth = rng.randint(0, 5)
    for _ in range(depth):
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            parts.append(rng.choice(DIR_PARTS))
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_component(rng))

    # Filename
    fname = _rand_component(rng)
    # Choose extension to guide libspectre behavior
    if rng.random() < 0.85:
        fname += _rand_ext(rng)
    parts.append(fname)

    # Optionally insert duplicate slashes and dot components while keeping validity
    sep = "/"
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        sep = "//"

    path = prefix + sep.join(parts)

    # Optionally add trailing spaces or case variations (still valid on POSIX)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        path = path.replace("PS", "Ps")

    # Ensure non-empty
    if not path:
        path = "file.ps"

    # Limit length
    if len(path) > 4000:
        path = path[:4000]

    return path

def _choose_mode(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # The harness provides an existing temporary path for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. Sometimes we want
    # a path-like token that looks like a file in CWD, sometimes an absolute temp-like path.
    return rng.choice(["relative", "absolute", "cwd", "nested"])

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    mode = _choose_mode(rng)

    # Build the base path according to mode
    if mode == "absolute":
        path = _build_path(rng)
        if not path.startswith("/"):
            path = "/" + path.lstrip("/")
    elif mode == "cwd":
        # Single basename in current directory
        name = _rand_component(rng)
        if rng.random() < 0.9:
            name += _rand_ext(rng)
        path = name
    elif mode == "nested":
        # Deeper hierarchy to exercise directory handling
        depth = rng.randint(2, 6)
        parts = [_rand_component(rng) for _ in range(depth)]
        parts[-1] += _rand_ext(rng)
        path = "/".join(parts)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            path = "/" + path
    else:  # relative
        path = _build_path(rng)
        if path.startswith("/"):
            path = path.lstrip("/")

    # Optionally add a .pdf target to exercise exporter_begin/save paths distinctly
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        root, _, _ext = path.rpartition('.')
        if root:
            path = root + ".pdf"

    # Ensure <= 4096 bytes and valid UTF-8 capable; if not, fallback ASCII
    try:
        data = path.encode('utf-8')
    except UnicodeEncodeError:
        path = ''.join(ch if ord(ch) < 128 else '_' for ch in path)
        data = path.encode('ascii')

    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    return data

import random
import struct
from typing import Tuple

# This generator creates valid PostScript/EPS data tailored for Libspectre loaders.
# Strategy:
# - Emit a DSC-compliant header with either PS or EPS variants.
# - Provide required DSC comments like %%Pages, %%BoundingBox, %%EndComments.
# - Include simple drawing commands that exercise different operators, text, paths, images.
# - Optionally include multiple pages with showpage, or EPS without showpage semantics.
# - Randomize rotation/scale and content to trigger different parsing/rendering paths.
# - Keep total size under 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministically random given a seed.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

PS_PROLOGUE = [
    "%%!PS-Adobe-3.0\n",
    "%%Creator: fuzzgen\n",
    "%%Title: Fuzzed Document\n",
    "%%LanguageLevel: {ll}\n",
    "%%Pages: {pages}\n",
    "%%BoundingBox: {bb}\n",
    "%%EndComments\n",
]

EPS_PROLOGUE = [
    "%%!PS-Adobe-3.0 EPSF-3.0\n",
    "%%Creator: fuzzgen\n",
    "%%Title: Fuzzed EPS\n",
    "%%LanguageLevel: {ll}\n",
    "%%BoundingBox: {bb}\n",
    "%%EndComments\n",
]

PAGE_TEMPLATE_BEGIN = [
    "%%Page: {num} {num}\n",
    "gsave\n",
]

PAGE_TEMPLATE_END = [
    "grestore\n",
    "showpage\n",
]

# Simple content building blocks

def ps_set_rgb(r: float, g: float, b: float) -> str:
    return f"{r:.3f} {g:.3f} {b:.3f} setrgbcolor\n"

def ps_rect(x: float, y: float, w: float, h: float, fill: bool) -> str:
    cmds = [
        f"{x:.1f} {y:.1f} moveto\n",
        f"{w:.1f} 0 rlineto\n",
        f"0 {h:.1f} rlineto\n",
        f"{-w:.1f} 0 rlineto\n",
        "closepath\n",
    ]
    cmds.append("fill\n" if fill else "stroke\n")
    return "".join(cmds)


def ps_circle(cx: float, cy: float, r: float, fill: bool) -> str:
    # Approximate circle with Bezier curve using arc operator for simplicity
    cmds = [f"newpath {cx:.1f} {cy:.1f} {r:.1f} 0 360 arc\n", "closepath\n"]
    cmds.append("fill\n" if fill else "stroke\n")
    return "".join(cmds)


def ps_text(x: float, y: float, size: float, text: str) -> str:
    safe = text.replace("(", "\\(").replace(")", "\\)")
    return f"/Helvetica findfont {size:.1f} scalefont setfont {x:.1f} {y:.1f} moveto ({safe}) show\n"


def ps_transform(scale: float, rot: int, tx: float, ty: float) -> str:
    return f"{tx:.1f} {ty:.1f} translate {rot} rotate {scale:.3f} {scale:.3f} scale\n"


def ps_image(width: int, height: int, gray: bool) -> str:
    # Emit a tiny inline image using image (grayscale) or colorimage (RGB)
    # Keep data short to remain under size limits; use hex strings.
    w = max(1, min(width, 32))
    h = max(1, min(height, 32))
    if gray:
        comps = 1
        head = f"{w} {h} 8 [{w} 0 0 -{h} 0 {h}]\n" \
               f"{{<"
        # generate w*h bytes
        data = bytes((i * 37 + 53) % 256 for i in range(w * h))
        hexdata = data.hex()
        tail = ">} image\n"
        return head + hexdata + tail
    else:
        comps = 3
        head = f"{w} {h} 8 [{w} 0 0 -{h} 0 {h}]\n" \
               f"{{<"
        data = bytes((i * 17 + j * 29) % 256 for i in range(w * h) for j in range(3))
        hexdata = data.hex()
        tail = ">} false 3 colorimage\n"
        return head + hexdata + tail


def random_bbox(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    # Keep box within typical ranges
    llx = rng.choice([0, 10, 36])
    lly = rng.choice([0, 10, 36])
    urx = rng.choice([300, 400, 595, 612])
    ury = rng.choice([300, 400, 842, 792])
    if urx <= llx + 10:
        urx = llx + 100
    if ury <= lly + 10:
        ury = lly + 100
    return llx, lly, urx, ury


def build_prologue(rng: random.Random, pages: int, eps: bool) -> str:
    ll = rng.choice([1, 2, 3])
    bb = random_bbox(rng)
    bb_str = f"{bb[0]} {bb[1]} {bb[2]} {bb[3]}"
    if eps:
        lines = [l.format(ll=ll, bb=bb_str) for l in EPS_PROLOGUE]
    else:
        lines = [l.format(ll=ll, pages=pages, bb=bb_str) for l in PS_PROLOGUE]
    # Add a compact prolog to exercise dictionaries and procedures
    prolog = [
        "%%BeginProlog\n",
        "/bx { % x y w h f r g b -- draw box\n",
        "    /b exch def /g exch def /r exch def /f exch def /h exch def /w exch def /y exch def /x exch def\n",
        "    gsave r g b setrgbcolor x y moveto w 0 rlineto 0 h rlineto w neg 0 rlineto closepath\n",
        "    f 0 ne { fill } { stroke } ifelse grestore\n",
        "} bind def\n",
        "%%EndProlog\n",
    ]
    return "".join(lines + prolog)


def build_page(rng: random.Random, num: int, bb: Tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> str:
    llx, lly, urx, ury = bb
    w = urx - llx
    h = ury - lly
    lines = [l.format(num=num) for l in PAGE_TEMPLATE_BEGIN]

    # Random transform
    scale = rng.uniform(0.5, 2.0)
    rot = rng.choice([0, 90, 180, 270])
    tx = rng.uniform(llx, llx + w * 0.2)
    ty = rng.uniform(lly, lly + h * 0.2)
    lines.append(ps_transform(scale, rot, tx, ty))

    # Background rectangle
    lines.append(ps_set_rgb(rng.random(), rng.random(), rng.random()))
    lines.append(ps_rect(20, 20, w * 0.4, h * 0.3, fill=True))

    # Stroked circle
    lines.append(ps_set_rgb(0, 0, 0))
    lines.append("2 setlinewidth\n")
    lines.append(ps_circle(w * 0.25, h * 0.25, min(w, h) * 0.1, fill=False))

    # Text
    txt = rng.choice([
        "Hello, Libspectre",
        "Page "+str(num),
        "EPS/PS fuzz",
        "Rotation "+str(rot),
    ])
    lines.append(ps_text(30, h * 0.15, rng.uniform(8, 24), txt))

    # Small inline image (sometimes grayscale, sometimes RGB)
    gray = rng.choice([True, False])
    lines.append("gsave\n")
    lines.append(f"{w*0.1:.1f} {h*0.1:.1f} translate {w*0.005:.3f} {h*0.005:.3f} scale\n")
    lines.append(ps_image(rng.randint(4, 16), rng.randint(4, 16), gray))
    lines.append("grestore\n")

    lines.extend(PAGE_TEMPLATE_END)
    return "".join(lines)


def build_eps_body(rng: random.Random, bb: Tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> str:
    llx, lly, urx, ury = bb
    w = urx - llx
    h = ury - lly
    lines = ["gsave\n"]
    # Fit content into bbox
    lines.append(ps_transform(rng.uniform(0.6, 1.6), rng.choice([0, 90, 180, 270]), 0, 0))
    # Use the custom bx proc
    r, g, b = rng.random(), rng.random(), rng.random()
    lines.append(f"50 50 {w*0.5:.1f} {h*0.35:.1f} 1 {r:.3f} {g:.3f} {b:.3f} bx\n")
    lines.append(ps_text(60, h * 0.2, rng.uniform(9, 22), "EPS body"))
    lines.append(ps_set_rgb(0.1, 0.1, 0.1))
    lines.append("1 setlinewidth\n")
    # Polyline
    lines.append("newpath 10 10 moveto 80 30 lineto 120 15 lineto 180 60 lineto stroke\n")
    # Image
    lines.append("gsave 20 20 translate 3 3 scale\n")
    lines.append(ps_image(rng.randint(6, 14), rng.randint(6, 14), gray=rng.choice([True, False])))
    lines.append("grestore\n")
    lines.append("grestore\n")
    return "".join(lines)


def assemble_document(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    eps = rng.choice([True, False])
    pages = rng.randint(1, 3) if not eps else 0
    # Fix bbox early for consistent layout across pages
    bb = random_bbox(rng)
    pro = build_prologue(rng, pages=pages, eps=eps)
    body = []
    if eps:
        body.append(build_eps_body(rng, bb))
    else:
        for p in range(1, pages + 1):
            body.append(build_page(rng, p, bb))
        body.append("%%Trailer\n%%EOF\n")
    doc = pro + "".join(body)

    # Trim to size limit while keeping validity; prefer trimming trailing binary (none here)
    b = doc.encode("ascii", errors="ignore")
    if len(b) > MAX_SIZE:
        b = b[:MAX_SIZE]
        # Ensure we end at a line boundary to avoid truncating tokens mid-word
        last_nl = b.rfind(b"\n")
        if last_nl > 0:
            b = b[:last_nl+1]
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return assemble_document(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces interesting, valid arbitrary strings intended to be used
# as labels for spectre_document_get_page_by_label. The fuzzer stub requires a
# non-empty NUL-terminated string (no embedded NULs). We therefore craft a variety
# of plausible PostScript/EPS-like page labels and common document label patterns
# (numbers, roman numerals, alphanumerics, section-like labels, unicode-ish ASCII
# approximations), while keeping bytes under 4096.

_MAX_LEN = 512  # Keep well under 4096 overall

_ROMAN = [
    "i","ii","iii","iv","v","vi","vii","viii","ix","x",
    "xi","xii","xiii","xiv","xv","xvi","xvii","xviii","xix","xx",
]

_ALNUM_SETS: List[str] = [
    string.ascii_uppercase,
    string.ascii_lowercase,
    string.digits,
    string.ascii_letters,
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits,
]

_PREFIXES = [
    "Page ", "PAGE ", "page ", "P", "p", "Pg ", "Sheet ", "Slide ",
    "Sec ", "Section ", "Part ", "Fig ", "Table ", "A", "B", "C",
]

_SUFFIXES = [
    "", "A", "B", "C", "-A", "-B", "-C", " (front)", " (back)",
    "-recto", "-verso", ".1", ".2", ".3"
]

_WORDS = [
    "Title", "Abstract", "Intro", "Introduction", "Methods", "Results",
    "Discussion", "Conclusion", "Appendix", "Index", "Cover", "TOC",
    "Glossary", "References", "Acknowledgements",
]

# Some typical label formats

def _decimal_label(r: random.Random) -> str:
    n = r.randint(0, 9999)
    return str(n)


def _zero_padded_label(r: random.Random) -> str:
    width = r.choice([2,3,4,5])
    n = r.randint(0, 10**width - 1)
    return f"{n:0{width}d}"


def _roman_label(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Random roman up to 3999 by naive composition
    val = r.randint(1, 3999)
    numerals = [
        (1000, "M"), (900, "CM"), (500, "D"), (400, "CD"),
        (100, "C"), (90, "XC"), (50, "L"), (40, "XL"),
        (10, "X"), (9, "IX"), (5, "V"), (4, "IV"), (1, "I"),
    ]
    out = []
    for v, sym in numerals:
        while val >= v:
            out.append(sym)
            val -= v
    # Randomly lower-case sometimes
    s = "".join(out)
    return s if r.random() < 0.6 else s.lower()


def _alpha_series_label(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # A, B, ..., Z, AA, AB, ...
    n = r.randint(1, 702)  # 1..26 + 26*26
    def to_alpha(num: int) -> str:
        num0 = num - 1
        if num0 < 26:
            return chr(ord('A') + num0)
        return chr(ord('A') + (num0 // 26) - 1) + chr(ord('A') + (num0 % 26))
    s = to_alpha(n)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        s = s.lower()
    return s


def _compound_label(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # e.g., "Section 3.2", "Part II-B", "Page 12A", etc.
    typ = r.randint(0, 5)
    if typ == 0:
        return f"Section {_decimal_label(r)}.{r.randint(0,9)}"
    if typ == 1:
        return f"Part {_roman_label(r)}-{_alpha_series_label(r).upper()}"
    if typ == 2:
        return f"Page {_zero_padded_label(r)}{r.choice(_SUFFIXES)}"
    if typ == 3:
        return f"{r.choice(_WORDS)}"
    if typ == 4:
        return f"{r.choice(_PREFIXES)}{_decimal_label(r)}"
    return f"{_alpha_series_label(r)}-{_decimal_label(r)}"


def _random_alnum(r: random.Random) -> str:
    length = r.randint(1, min(40, _MAX_LEN))
    alphabet = r.choice(_ALNUM_SETS)
    # Occasionally include separators
    seps = "-_.:/ "
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        alphabet += seps
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    # Avoid leading/trailing spaces
    return s.strip() or "x"


def _mix_with_prefix_suffix(r: random.Random, core: str) -> str:
    pre = r.choice(["", r.choice(_PREFIXES)])
    suf = r.choice(["", r.choice(_SUFFIXES)])
    candidate = (pre + core + suf).strip()
    return candidate if candidate else core


def _bounded(s: str) -> str:
    # Ensure length within bounds and non-empty, without NULs.
    s = s.replace("\x00", "")
    if not s:
        s = "x"
    if len(s) > _MAX_LEN:
        s = s[:_MAX_LEN]
    return s


def _choose_label(r: random.Random) -> str:
    makers = [
        _decimal_label,
        _zero_padded_label,
        _roman_label,
        _alpha_series_label,
        _compound_label,
        _random_alnum,
    ]
    # Bias towards structured labels
    weights = [2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 1]
    maker = r.choices(makers, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    core = maker(r)
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        core = _mix_with_prefix_suffix(r, core)
    # Sometimes add small hierarchical parts: e.g., "3-2" or "II.A"
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        joiner = r.choice(["-", ".", ":", " "])
        extra = r.choice([_decimal_label(r), _alpha_series_label(r), _roman_label(r)])
        core = f"{core}{joiner}{extra}"
    # Sometimes include parentheses or brackets
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        wrap = r.choice([("(", ")"), ("[", "]"), ("{", "}"), ("<", ">")])
        core = f"{wrap[0]}{core}{wrap[1]}"
    return _bounded(core)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Create a small corpus of varied labels; pick one deterministically from seed
    candidates: List[str] = []
    count = r.randint(1, 8)  # produce 1..8 variants and pick one to return
    for _ in range(count):
        candidates.append(_choose_label(r))
    # Choose one candidate to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR; ensure non-empty and ASCII
    choice = r.choice(candidates)
    # Ensure no NULs and printable range; keep as bytes via utf-8 (ASCII subset)
    choice = _bounded(choice)
    data = choice.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if not data:
        data = b"x"
    # Return as bytes buffer (no trailing NUL; fuzzer will NUL-terminate internally)
    return data
